title: Search Bar Suggestions
statement: An online store has 500,000 product names. As a customer types, the search bar must show up to five names that start with what has been typed, after every key press.

approaches.name: A trie whose nodes keep the top five names below them
approaches.label: best
approaches.time: O(L) per key press after building
approaches.why: Each key press is one step down and a ready list.

approaches.name: Sort the names and binary search the first match for each prefix
approaches.label: valid
approaches.time: O(L log n) per key press
approaches.why: Also fast and simpler to store; a little slower per key press.

approaches.name: Check every name with startsWith on each key press
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Half a million checks for every letter typed.

approaches.name: A hash set of names
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Answers only exact names, not prefixes.

title: Chat Word Filter
statement: A game chat must find every blocked word (from a list of 10,000) inside each message as it is sent. Messages are up to 500 characters.

approaches.name: A trie of blocked words; from each message position, walk the trie as far as it goes
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Shared prefixes are checked once, and a walk stops as soon as no blocked word continues.

approaches.name: Aho–Corasick automaton
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Fastest, but more complex to build than needed here.

approaches.name: Run indexOf for every blocked word
approaches.label: unsuitable

approaches.name: Split the message on spaces and look words up in a hash set
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Misses blocked words hidden inside longer words.

title: Router Address Lookup
statement: A network router has 100,000 address prefixes (bit strings up to 32 bits) and must pick, for each incoming address, the longest prefix that matches it.

approaches.name: A binary trie of prefixes; walk the address bits and remember the last prefix end seen
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Constant time per address, however many prefixes.

approaches.name: A hash set per prefix length, checked from 32 down
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also bounded, but each step hashes; slower in practice.

approaches.name: Compare the address with every prefix
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Far too slow at millions of lookups.

approaches.name: Sort prefixes by length and take the first match
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Still scans the whole list for each address.
